summary: SL-008 added the 'Rescan as administrator' offer. A pure App file (RescanAsAdministrator.cs) decides the offer and starts the runas relaunch. A new Core.Native GlobalDosDevices keeps SUBST, mapped and UNC letters from being offered. The button sits on the pickers' line, and the report gains additive schema-1 keys. The product code drew no defect in any code-review pass. Nearly all rework (build 2, code-review passes 1 to 4) went into fitness.yaml patterns and guard tests that stop a later edit from reaching Start by another spelling. The UAC press itself and a real elevated read were never run: they are person-run (SC-085), and O-001 and O-002 were waived.

payload.summary: SL-008 added the 'Rescan as administrator' offer. A pure App file (RescanAsAdministrator.cs) decides the offer and starts the runas relaunch. A new Core.Native GlobalDosDevices keeps SUBST, mapped and UNC letters from being offered. The button sits on the pickers' line, and the report gains additive schema-1 keys. The product code drew no defect in any code-review pass. Nearly all rework (build 2, code-review passes 1 to 4) went into fitness.yaml patterns and guard tests that stop a later edit from reaching Start by another spelling. The UAC press itself and a real elevated read were never run: they are person-run (SC-085), and O-001 and O-002 were waived.

learned.lesson: When a finding's fix is a text-pattern rule over an open-ended spelling family, do not prescribe the literal regex at critique time. Require the class corpus with a 'before' column (as RescanElevationRulesCorpus.json has) first, or require a structural guard. Three of the critique's prescribed fixes (M2, m2, m3) were holes. Each closure then moved the boundary by one spelling: global:: (O-023), the Start( lookahead (O-026), a project-file <Using> item, a member in the excepted file, a qualified self-call or method group.
learned.evidence: fitness.yaml:1640-1647 call-site entry. Class reopened in code-review #1 and #3 of 4. Corpus rows E17-E35 (19 rows) were added only in build 2. Open as SC-086, SC-087 and N-082.

learned.lesson: Fitness blanks comments but the SL-008 guard tests and corpus read raw text, so a comment anywhere in src outside RescanAsAdministrator.cs and MainWindow.xaml.cs fails the rule if it spells runas, UseShellExecute, ShellExecute*, RescanAsAdministrator.Start or OnRescanAsAdministrator. The fitness 'because' text at .taad/fitness.yaml:1612 wrongly says a comment may name them. The next slice that edits src or the hook must avoid those words in comments, including Kernel32.cs and Core.Native.
learned.evidence: Comment fixer left in code-review attempt 2: RescanElevationRulesCorpusTests.TheTreeDoesNotTripTheRulesTheCorpusRuns runs the patterns over raw text. The critique's m3 fix note warned a MainWindow comment naming ShellExecuteEx would fail the gate.

learned.lesson: The offer's trigger is ScanResult.Unreadable.Count > 0 with no look at the code or the path. System Volume Information is refused to a limited token on every NTFS volume, so a healthy whole-drive scan will almost always offer. SVI also stays unread under an admin token (SYSTEM-only ACL), so the elevated copy may recover nothing, and the elevated copy never offers again. Whether the offer pays off on a healthy drive was not settled, because the report carries counts only.
learned.evidence: Design decision 3 in design-slice-1.json. Spike elevated-rescan-reads-what-acl-allows: 6 residue folders under elevation, SVI among them, icacls shows SYSTEM only. The SL-008 script's whole-D: run gave 2 unread and offered=true, with 'whether SVI is one of D:'s 2 unread folders' not reached (validations#256).

learned.lesson: This Sandbox has EnableLUA=0, so any experiment that needs a UAC split token (same-account limited vs elevated) cannot run there as found. The subst spike got a real linked pair only by setting EnableLUA=1 and restarting the Sandbox VM (phase 2 after the restart). The harness then reported TIMEOUT while the result file still landed in the host out folder. The one claim the user cares about, that the same account's elevated token reads folders its limited token could not, has only a proxy measurement: two different accounts, 72 recovered, 6 residue, 0 newly failed.
learned.evidence: spikes#191: elevated-rescan-reads-what-acl-allows gate unmet (fsaadm LIMITED and HIGHEST both gave S-1-16-12288 type 1). subst-letter-invisible-to-linked-elevated-token ran only after the EnableLUA=1 restart.

learned.lesson: Size this project's slices by guard surface, not product surface. Product code was medium and passed code review with no defect. The surface was large: 2 fitness entries plus manifest and hook entries, 2 corpora, 7 new test files, and a new window script with a 44-row -Stub corpus. That matched lesson #897's 3+ laps and cost 4 code-review passes and 2 builds. Most of the other stage re-runs (critique, design, spike, validate halts) were waits on a decision, not rework.
learned.evidence: build #1 changed 23 files (e8626f2c), build #2 changed 10 (9761118e). Code-review #1 and #3 halted on guard-rule classes. Review #2 and #4 only disposed findings.

learned.lesson: A -Stub corpus plus MUTATE markers in an ending-table script (tests/window/SL-008-RescanOfferEndingsCorpus.json, 44 rows, run under pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1) proves a verdict-table fix. A copy of the script with the MUTATE lines removed fails rows M01-M04. Use it for the next window script. Two limits: the stub replaces the privilege read, so a privilege-definition mismatch (IsInRole(Administrator) vs the app's IsPrivilegedProcess token elevation) cannot be held by the corpus. And liveness after 6 s is not a 'no prompt' measurement.
learned.evidence: O-019 closure. N-081 (privilege definitions differ). N-079 and N-080 (ALIVE reported as held with no prompt).

learned.lesson: A whole-drive report-mode scan of this PC's D: (a Fixed, global letter, about 230 GB used) finished in well under 90 s with 2 unread folders and offered=true. The design's 3600 s bound for SL-008-RescanOfferOnALocalDrive.Tests.ps1 was a guess and is far too loose. The validator ran the same script with -DriveTimeoutSec 900 and the whole run, publish included, took about 32 s.
learned.evidence: builds#419 (script run 32 s). Build #1 ran it with a 90 s bound and it held. Validate ran it with -DriveTimeoutSec 900.

learned.lesson: The engine's own measure showed code review left 8 of 19 and then 9 of 9 changed files not read whole in this slice. That included .taad/fitness.yaml (seen only through Grep lines), the artefact the review was about. The real findings still came from repro tests run against the patterns. For a slice whose main artefact is a fitness entry, the review has to run its patterns on crafted input, and has to read the entry block whole.
learned.evidence: reviews#667 'not read (measured)' list. Lesson #914 (input-driven second pass) held again.

candidates.title: Offer 'Rescan as administrator' only when an elevated scan could read at least one of the unread folders
candidates.why: Offers/WorthProbing in src/FsAnalyser.App/RescanAsAdministrator.cs trigger on Unreadable.Count > 0 whatever the code or path (design decision 3). System Volume Information is refused to a limited token on every NTFS volume, and stays unread under an admin token (spike elevated-rescan-reads-what-acl-allows: 6 residue folders including SVI, ACL SYSTEM only). A healthy whole-drive scan can therefore offer a UAC prompt and a full rescan that recovers nothing. Measured on this PC: whole-D: report run gave 2 unread and offered=true (validations#256). Whether SVI is one of those 2 was not reached, because the report holds counts, never names. Check SC-085's press result first. Then narrow the trigger by reason code (UnreadableRows.PlainPhrase, UnreadableRows.cs:216-226: access denied 5/65 only) and drop a root-level System Volume Information. Do not offer for in-use (32) or cloud (362/363) codes.

candidates.title: Replace the regex call-site guards for RescanAsAdministrator.Start with one compiled-assembly call-graph test
candidates.why: The 'only the button's Click reaches Start' invariant is held by text patterns: the call-site entry at .taad/fitness.yaml:1640-1647, RescanElevationGuardTests, and RescanElevationRulesCorpus.json (115 lines; rows E17-E35, 19 of them, added in build 2). Code review reopened the class in passes 1 and 3 of 4: global:: and forwarder (pass 1); <Using> item, excepted-file member and qualified self-call or method group (pass 3). Pieces are waived as SC-087, N-082 and N-083. A check on the built App assembly (every call site of RescanAsAdministrator.Start must be MainWindow.OnRescanAsAdministrator; nothing else calls that handler or builds a runas ProcessStartInfo) sees through any spelling and would let those items be dropped. Not tried here: whether Core.Tests can read the built App dll (System.Reflection.Metadata is in the shared framework). Restore here uses the local package cache only (lesson #908), so a Roslyn package is not assured.

missed.what: The M2 fix (critic's own corrected patterns) used '[\w.]*' between 'using static' or 'using X =' and RescanAsAdministrator. It misses 'global::', an extern-alias qualifier and spaced dots, and the guard test copy hard-coded the same two regexes. A bare Start(...) from OnLoaded then passed both layers. The critique did not ask what other legal C# spellings reach a static member.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 (repro failed 3 of 3); closed in build 2 at fitness.yaml:1645-1646 (O-023)

missed.what: The M2 fix reads src/**/*.cs only and excepts MainWindow.xaml.cs and RescanAsAdministrator.cs as whole files. With ImplicitUsings on (Directory.Build.props:5), a <Using Include=...RescanAsAdministrator Static="true"> item in a project file reaches Start unseen. A second member of the excepted file that builds its own runas ProcessStartInfo is also unseen. The critique did not ask what the file-level exceptions cover beyond the one handler.
missed.caught_by: code-review #3 (repro failed 3 of 3 for <Using>); waived to SC-087 and N-082

missed.what: The m3 family ban ('Elevation:Administrator' only) leaves out the COM moniker's second documented level, 'Elevation:Highest!new:{clsid}', which elevates with no verb. The critique asked for a family ban but pinned one moniker spelling.

The m2 fix told the script to decide 'privileged' by IsInRole(Administrator) or IsSystem. The design and the app decide 'elevated' by Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess, which is token elevation. An elevated token without Administrators (for example Backup Operators) makes the script report FAILED where no offer is correct. The finding itself named IsPrivilegedProcess and the fix swapped it out.

Design case 13 says 'started with no path, with a path, ... no prompt', but the window steps can only observe that the process is alive at 6 s. A runas raised early on the window launch path blocks the UI thread on the prompt and still reads 'held, with no prompt'. Only a manifest-level 740 can fail those steps. The critique caught the same weakness for the report-mode step (M1 fix critic) but not for the window steps.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 (m2 and IN-m5); waived as N-079 and N-080

payload.estimate_error: Opened medium risk, medium size (sized by a person); the design kept it medium. Right for the product code: the offer, the probe and Start needed no change after review. Wrong on the surface: guard rules, two corpora, 7 test files and a stub-able script with 44 corpus rows. Lesson #897 predicts 3+ review laps for that, and it took 4 code-review passes and 2 builds, nearly all on the Start call-site guard. The other re-runs (critique, design, risk-spike, validate) were halts waiting on a decision, not rework.
what_went_wrong: Code review ran 4 times and the slice was built twice, almost entirely on one class: spellings that reach RescanAsAdministrator.Start without spelling it. Each closure moved the boundary one spelling (global::, the Start( lookahead, a project-file <Using>, the excepted file, a qualified self-call or method group). Three pieces ended waived (SC-086, SC-087, N-082), so the class is knowingly left open. Review found no defect in RescanAsAdministrator.cs, GlobalDosDevices or MainWindow.

The critique prescribed literal regexes or reads for M2, m2 and m3. Three of those fixes were holes (global::, the moniker's second level, a privilege definition that differs from the app's). Critique-review was sized out (medium, one designer), so nothing re-read the prescribed fixes before build.

The design again cited planted E005 scripts and tests that do not exist (critique M1, major), the same trap as lessons #876 and #896. The builder replaced them with RescanAsAdministratorOfferTests and the SL-008 script, and the cases were retargeted.

Risk-spike #1 hit an unmet gate (Sandbox EnableLUA=0) although lesson #24 says elevated experiments fail here. The claim that matters most, that the same account's elevated token reads what its limited token could not, has only a two-account proxy. The 'built anyway' note after spike #2 also says the design enables SeBackupPrivilege, but the design decided it does not.
The window script reports 'held ... with no prompt' for a process still alive after 6 s, which measures nothing about a prompt (N-079 and N-080, waived). O-015's discharge text repeats the claim.
Code review left 8 of 19 and then 9 of 9 changed files not read whole, .taad/fitness.yaml (the artefact under review) among them. The real findings came from repro tests, not the diff read.
The 'because' text at .taad/fitness.yaml:1612 says a comment may name the banned spellings, but the guard tests read raw text and a comment fails them. The comment fixer left it.

Validation could not reach the UAC press, a real elevated read on C: or D:, criterion 14 (a second scan in the same window, read only), or the identity of D:'s 2 unread folders. All of these sit in SC-085, N-084 and N-085.
unknowns: Does an elevated rescan of this PC's D: or C: read any folder the limited scan left unread, or are the unread ones only System Volume Information and other SYSTEM-only folders? The report carries counts only, so it was never seen.
Does Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess read true, and the offer stay hidden, in a copy started through a real UAC consent as an administrator? Measured only as SYSTEM in the Sandbox (criterion 8).
Does a session-local DefineDosDevice definition over C: or D: (letter shadowing, IN-m4, O-001) make the elevated copy scan a different volume from the one that offered?
Does a real interactive consent elevation see the same GLOBAL?? letters as the LogonUserW token pair, and does EnableLinkedConnections=1 change that (N-074, N-075)?
Does the second scan in the same window after an offered ending (pressed or not) hide the button and clear the status line (criterion 14)? Only StartScan's HideRescanOffer was read.

lessons_judged.why: The slice asked no count question about C:\ unreadable folders; it used a drive-letter probe and the SL-008 script's D: run.
Validation listed real C: and D: elevated reads as 'not reached' and did not cite the whole-drive shape as validated; the exe-level check used D:.
The probe takes injected typeOf and holdsLetter readers; a Network letter is never opened and no default test touches Z:\.
Sandbox-as-SYSTEM facts drove critique m1 (a SUBST letter made by SYSTEM is global). The SUBST asserts became HoldsDriveLetter == IsSystem, and validation ran the UNC and SYSTEM cases in the Sandbox.
No Scanner.Run.FolderDone change. The slice only relied on SL-005 having removed vanished folders from Unreadable.
The button and RescanStatus went on the pickers' line (one button tall) instead of OutcomeTexts, which is capped at 76 px; PickerPanel's height is compared in the script.
The UAC press was filed as a person check (SC-085) and kept out of the loop's validation. Risk-spike #1 still tried an elevated experiment and ended gate-unmet, so the lesson held again.
The same principle: the press criterion was marked person-run when the slice opened, so validate passed with O-001 and O-002 waived instead of looping on an unreachable prompt.
The slice again stacked UI, native interop and a human-only elevation dependency, but the rework came from the call-site guard rules, not from that stacking; product code passed review first time.
The person-run part (the press) was split off as SC-085 at open, so the loop closed the code on loop evidence.
No new no-path state was read; the script's no-path launch checks liveness only.
The design reused the launch-with-a-path route and did not edit App.xaml.cs, and said so to keep the tests/bugs guard out of play.

The code review's input-driven pass (crafted using-spellings, the monikers, real repro tests) found every finding that mattered. The engine again measured many files not read whole (8 of 19, then 9 of 9).
The SL-008 script's scratch is rooted under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp as the design said.
It predicted this exactly: a new window script plus fitness.yaml edits took 4 code-review passes. It did not change the medium sizing, so it was confirmed rather than applied.
Every review and the validator ran Fitness op=check (120 rules) and ArchitectureRulesTests; the build's green tests alone were not trusted for fitness.
This repo's checks use eng/dotnet.ps1 test with xUnit filters; the scripts/test.ps1 -q pytest form in the lesson does not exist here.
The elevated-rescan spike named its expected residue (SVI and a few SYSTEM-only folders) and the 72/6/0 result fell within it. The SUBST no-go was still routed as 'built anyway'.
The class-corpus-with-a-before-column oracle was copied for the elevation rules: RescanElevationRulesCorpus.json, 56 rows in build 1, E17-E35 added in build 2.
The Windows-path alias classes (SUBST, UNC, \\?\, lowercase letters, trailing backslash) were enumerated in the Offers and probe tests. The slice needed 1 design lap, not 4.
The builder wrote SL-008-*.Tests.ps1 instead of the absent E005 files and listed it as a non-launcher. The design had still cited the absent files, which was critique M1.
Critique M1 applied it: git ls-files for E005 found nothing, so the cases were retargeted to builder-owned checks. The design again skipped the check before citing the files.
The offer was kept out of OutcomeTexts, and the report reads RescanAsAdministratorButton as visible and inView.
The probe tests use the shared SubstDrive helper for the session-local letter case.
The full suite was run with -- xUnit.MaxParallelThreads=2 and free memory was checked first, as the lesson says.

filed.title: Check by hand: Pressing it relaunches the app elevated through the UAC prompt and scans the same root
